claim: Chloride regulates the autophosphorylation and activity of the WNK1 and WNK3 kinase domains.
source: Osmotic stress and chloride regulate the autophosphorylation and activity of the WNK1 and WNK3 kinase domains.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about WNK kinase regulation.

claim: The kinase domain of unphosphorylated WNK1 (uWNK1) is an asymmetric dimer.
source: The kinase domain of unphosphorylated WNK1 (uWNK1) is an asymmetric dimer possessing water molecules conserved in multiple uWNK1 crystal structures.

claim: Unphosphorylated WNK1 possesses water molecules conserved in multiple uWNK1 crystal structures.

claim: PEG400 applied to crystals of dimeric uWNK1 induces de-dimerization.
source: Here, we show that PEG400 applied to crystals of dimeric uWNK1 induces de-dimerization.

claim: Both the WNK1 water networks and the chloride-binding site are disrupted by PEG400.

claim: The homologous mutation WNK1/E388A enhanced the rate of autophosphorylation and reduced chloride sensitivity.

claim: The water and chloride regulation appear linked.

claim: The lower activity of some mutants may reflect effects on catalysis.

claim: WNK kinases are noted for their unique active site.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ADP-Glo assay data with PEG400.

claim: At 0.8 mg/ml, wild-type uWNK3 exhibits an apparent mass of ~60 kD, suggestive of a 50/50 mixture of 40 kD monomer and 80 kD dimer.
source: At 0.8 mg/ml, wild-type uWNK3 exhibits an apparent mass of ~60 kD, suggestive of a 50/50 mixture of 40 kD monomer and 80 kD dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SLS data.

claim: At 1.8 mg/ml uWNK3 is dimeric.
source: At 1.8 mg/ml uWNK3 is dimeric.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SLS data.

claim: Wild-type uWNK1 is monomeric at both 0.8 mg/ml and 1.8 mg/ml concentrations.
source: In contrast, wild-type uWNK1 is monomeric at both concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SLS data.

claim: The WNK3 mutants generally exhibited 50/50 mixtures at 0.8 mg/ml, similar to wild-type uWNK3.
source: The WNK3 mutants generally exhibited 50/50 mixtures at 0.8 mg/ml, similar to wild-type uWNK3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SLS data.

claim: Two of the mutants, WNK3/E314Q and WNK3/D279N were monomeric.
source: Two of the mutants, WNK3/E314Q and WNK3/D279N were monomeric.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SLS data.

claim: The appearance of monomers on mutating the AL-CL Cluster support the idea that the waters in CWN1 promote the dimer.
source: The appearance of monomers on mutating the AL-CL Cluster support the idea that the waters in CWN1 promote the dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the SLS data.

claim: Crystals of WNK1/SA/E388A did not diffract.
source: Crystals of WNK1/SA/E388A did not diffract.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: WNK3/SA/E314A crystallized, affording limited diffraction to 3.4 Å.
source: WNK3/SA/E314A crystallized, affording limited diffraction to 3.4 Å (see Materials and methods and Supplementary file 1h).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on crystallographic data collection.

claim: WNK3/SA/E314A crystals were in space group P1, and adopts a unique dimer in which the Activation Loops are swapped.
source: WNK3/SA/E314A crystals were in space group P1, and adopts a unique dimer in which the Activation Loops are swapped.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on crystallographic structure determination.

claim: Excluding the Activation Loops, uWNK3/SA/E314A is more similar to uWNK1/SA/PEG400 than uWNK1/SA (with r.m.s.d.'s of 0.7 versus 0.85, respectively).
source: Excluding the Activation Loops, comparisons of uWNK3/SA/E314A, uWNK1/SA, and uWNK1/SA/PEG400 show that uWNK3/SA/E314A is more similar to uWNK1/SA/PEG400 than uWNK1/SA (with r.m.s.d.'s of 0.7 versus 0.85, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural comparison.

claim: The orientations of the 3/10 helix and helix C in uWNK3/SA/E314A most resemble WNK1/SA/PEG400.
source: Furthermore, the orientations of the 3/10 helix and helix C most resemble WNK1/SA/PEG400 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The greater similarity of uWNK3/SA/E314A to uWNK1/SA/PEG400 than to uWNK1/SA is apparent in the plot of conformational differences as a function of sequence.
source: The greater similarity of uWNK3/SA/E314A to uWNK1/SA/PEG400 than to uWNK1/SA is apparent in the plot of conformational differences as a function of sequence (blue trace smaller than cyan trace, Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: WNK kinases in cells are inhibited by chloride and activated by osmotic stress.
source: WNK kinases in cells are inhibited by chloride and activated by osmotic stress.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: WNK kinase domains exhibit multiple conformers.
source: WNK kinase domains exhibit multiple conformers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on crystallographic and SAXS data.

claim: Inactive forms of both WNK1 (crystallography) and WNK3 (SAXS data) form asymmetric dimers.
source: Inactive forms of both WNK1 (crystallography) and WNK3 (SAXS data) form asymmetric dimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on structural data.

claim: Prior data showed that chloride ion binds and promotes the inactive dimer.
source: Prior data showed that chloride ion binds and promotes the inactive dimer, whereas osmolytes, in vitro surrogates for osmotic pressure, de-dimerize WNK kinase domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by prior studies.

claim: Osmolytes, in vitro surrogates for osmotic pressure, de-dimerize WNK kinase domains.
source: Prior data showed that chloride ion binds and promotes the inactive dimer, whereas osmolytes, in vitro surrogates for osmotic pressure, de-dimerize WNK kinase domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by prior studies.

claim: Prior crystallographic data implicate a highly unique water-binding site, the AL-CL Cluster, in the inactive WNK1 dimer, as compared with typical protein kinases.
source: Prior crystallographic data implicate a highly unique water-binding site, the AL-CL Cluster, in the inactive WNK1 dimer, as compared with typical protein kinases.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on crystallographic data.

claim: Data presented here show that PEG400 applied to crystals of WNK1 rearranged and eliminated the AL-CL Cluster and the associated network of water molecules, CWN1.
source: Data presented here show that PEG400 applied to crystals of WNK1 rearranged and eliminated the AL-CL Cluster and the associated network of water molecules, CWN1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the crystallographic results.

claim: PEG400 also eliminated the chloride-binding site and all the waters in CWN2.
source: PEG400 also eliminated the chloride-binding site and all the waters in CWN2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the crystallographic results.

claim: The water networks can be allosteric ligands that promote the inactive structure of WNKs.
source: Apparently, the water networks can be allosteric ligands that promote the inactive structure of WNKs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Some AL-CL Cluster mutants, studied primarily in WNK3, were more monomeric than wild-type.
source: Some AL-CL Cluster mutants, studied primarily in WNK3, were more monomeric than wild-type.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on SLS data.

claim: Among the mutants assayed, WNK3/E314A,Q and WNK1/E388A exhibited enhanced activity.
source: Among the mutants assayed, WNK3/E314A,Q and WNK1/E388A exhibited enhanced activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on activity assay data.

claim: The enhanced activity of these mutants supports the hypothesis that the dimer is inhibitory and that CWN1 promotes the dimer.
source: The enhanced activity of these mutants supports the hypothesis that the dimer is inhibitory and that CWN1 promotes the dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the mutagenesis data.

claim: Crystallography of WNK3/E314A shows that it exhibits conformational differences at the same loci as observed by PEG400 applied to crystals of WNK1.
source: Crystallography of WNK3/E314A shows that it exhibits conformational differences at the same loci as observed by PEG400 applied to crystals of WNK1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on crystallographic comparison.

claim: Several mutants were less active than wild-type.
source: Several mutants were less active than wild-type.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on activity assay data.

claim: The mechanisms for the reduced activity are unclear.
source: The mechanisms for the reduced activity are unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion acknowledging uncertainty about the interpretation.

claim: Since the AL-CL Cluster and CWN1 are in the enzyme active site, reduced activity may be due to effects on substrate binding or catalysis.
source: However, since the AL-CL Cluster and CWN1 are in the enzyme active site, reduced activity may be due to effects on substrate binding or catalysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculative explanation.

claim: The activity and chloride sensitivity appear coupled in the AL-CL Cluster mutants.
source: First, the activity and chloride sensitivity appear coupled in the AL-CL Cluster mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on the observation of correlated changes in activity and chloride sensitivity.

claim: Mutants were either more active and less chloride sensitive, or less active and more chloride sensitive.
source: Mutants were either more active and less chloride sensitive, or less active and more chloride sensitive.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on activity and chloride sensitivity assay data.

claim: The less chloride-sensitive mutants can be understood as arising from destabilization of the chloride-binding helix and the dimer.
source: The less chloride-sensitive mutants can be understood as arising from destabilization of the chloride-binding helix and the dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: There is no interpretation so far for the enhanced chloride sensitivity of the low activity mutants.
source: We have no interpretation so far for the enhanced chloride sensitivity of the low activity mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion acknowledging a gap in understanding.

claim: ADP Glo assays showed a PEG-induced activation of substrate phosphorylation, consistent with the model.
source: Second, ADP Glo assays, compatible with the crowding agent PEG400, showed a PEG-induced activation of substrate phosphorylation, consistent with our model.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on ADP-Glo assay data.

claim: Among the active mutants, no single mutant abolished PEG sensitivity.
source: Among the active mutants, though, no single mutant abolished PEG sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on ADP-Glo assay data with PEG400.

claim: It has been posited recently that intracellular water potential is very tightly regulated in the face of osmotic and thermal stresses, and that water itself is the likely entity sensed to elicit responses.
source: It has been posited recently that intracellular water potential is very tightly regulated in the face of osmotic and thermal stresses, and that water itself is the likely entity sensed to elicit responses (Watson et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to Watson et al., 2023.

claim: The present structural data support the idea that water is directly sensed in WNKs.
source: The present structural data support the idea that water is directly sensed in WNKs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the crystallographic and mutagenesis data.

claim: Activation Loop phosphorylation at WNK3/S308 and WNK3/S304 is necessary for WNK activity.
source: Activation Loop phosphorylation at WNK3/S308 (WNK1/S382) and WNK3/S304 (WNK1/S378) is necessary for WNK activity (Xu et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to Xu et al., 2002.
